subject.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode — the roadmap

question: Should OpenClaw accept Codex-style structured questions, plan mode, and goal mode as core runtime features now, and should the linked implementation land as one broad branch or staged PRs?
rationale: The requested work changes cross-surface interaction, default tool exposure, goal continuation semantics, and channel/UI delivery, so automation cannot decide the intended product and rollout shape.

options.title: Split staged PRs
options.body: Keep this hub open and require staged review for the question pipeline, plan mode, and goal driver with focused proof for each surface.

options.title: Sponsor full branch
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the broad review cost and resolve proof, CI, and rollout concerns on the linked implementation branch.

options.title: Defer or narrow
options.body: Maintainers can keep only smaller follow-ups open if these primitives should wait or move behind a narrower design first.

recommendation.title: Split staged PRs
recommendation.body: Keep this hub open and require staged review for the question pipeline, plan mode, and goal driver with focused proof for each surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest merged-history signal across Codex user-input, update_plan policy, and core goal surfaces touched by the roadmap.
